title: Precision Switchover Safeguard Orchestrator for Quantized Rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an orchestration layer (Safeguard Orchestrator) that manages staged rollouts of FP8/INT8 quantized model variants with automated quality gates and deterministic fallback to higher-precision variants when accuracy/regression checks fail. Scope includes: calibration workflow integration (offline and live calibration traces), golden prompt set evaluation, rollout traffic shaping (percent steps, hold windows), and an automatic policy engine that can switch traffic or trigger rollback when a configurable set of checks cross thresholds. Non-goals: model training, new quantization algorithms, or UI polish beyond basic Console telemetry surfaces.
acceptance_criteria: Can deploy a quantized model as a staged rollout with configurable steps (default 0->5->25->50->100%) and hold windows per step
Automated evaluation runs against the golden prompt set produce pass/fail verdicts and a numeric regression score (token-F1, top-k match, embedding cosine) within each step

Policy engine triggers automatic fallback (traffic routed to FP16/FP32 variant) if any of: token-level divergence > 4% over window, embedding cosine drop > 0.03, hallucination rate increase > 2x, or latency percentiles exceed SLO by >20%
Fallback action is atomic and observable (Console event, alert, rollback PR created) and system can re-attempt a subsequent rollout after manual review
End-to-end e2e test harness simulates stochastic sampling and verifies fallback decisions in CI with mocked infra failure modes
Telemetry (per-route and per-token) surfaces in Console: rollout percentage, PSNR-style quality delta, calibration delta, and rollback audit log

release_notes: Adds Safeguard Orchestrator for quantized rollouts: staged traffic steps, automatic fallback policy DSL, and calibration-aware gating. Requires runtime-1.20 and Console telemetry v2.
notes: Design choices: (1) Use deterministic evaluation seeds for canary gates to avoid stochastic false positives; (2) Require 2-of-3 failing eval windows before triggering an automatic fallback to reduce sensitivity; (3) Provide per-customer overrides and an emergency manual rollback; (4) Keep calibration metadata immutable and attach to rollout artifacts for reproducibility.
